item.title: SoE Minister Duma to unveil PNG’s Sovereign Cloud and AI Datacenter
item.description: The Government of Papua New Guinea will mark a significant milestone in the country’s digital transformation journey on Friday, 21 August 2026, with the official inauguration of Kumul Cloud Infinity — PNG’s Sovereign Cloud and AI Datacenter, at the Sheraton Hotel, Port Moresby. The landmark facility, developed by Datec PNG and Telikom PNG, represents a major step towards strengthening Papua New Gu
item.content:encoded:
The Government of Papua New Guinea will mark a significant milestone in the country’s digital transformation journey on Friday, 21 August 2026, with the official inauguration of Kumul Cloud Infinity — PNG’s Sovereign Cloud and AI Datacenter, at the Sheraton Hotel, Port Moresby.

The landmark facility, developed by Datec PNG and Telikom PNG, represents a major step towards strengthening Papua New Guinea’s digital sovereignty, data security and national AI capabilities.

This will enable organisations to securely host, process and manage critical data and digital workloads within the country.

CEO of Datec PNG, Preetam Talukdar, said the launch represents a defining moment for both Datec and Papua New Guinea.

“Kumul Cloud Infinity is not simply a technology project. It is about sovereignty in its truest digital sense — giving Papua New Guinea the ability to control, protect and build upon its own digital future.”Talukdar said.

He said the initiative reflects Datec PNG and Telikom PNG’s commitment to investing in infrastructure that will enable Papua New Guineans, businesses and institutions to participate more confidently in the global digital economy.

Minister for State Enterprises, William Duma will lead the inauguration and unveil the new Kumul Cloud Infinity facility.

This new chapter in PNG’s digital sovereignty is to ensure that Papua New Guinea has the infrastructure and capability to own, control and protect its digital future.

Kumul Cloud Infinity is designed to provide a trusted in-country environment for cloud computing, artificial intelligence, data hosting, enterprise applications and other advanced digital workloads.

The initiative also brings together the capabilities of Datec PNG, Telikom PNG and international technology partners, creating a platform designed to support PNG’s growing digital economy and the next generation of technology-led businesses and services.

item.title: Buimo inmates graduate from pre-release training
item.description: One hundred inmates at Buimo Correctional Institution in Morobe graduated from a pre-release training program, equipping them with practical skills, knowledge and confidence for life after release. The program of eight weeks is aimed to support inmates to improve their livelihood opportunities, and reduce the risk of reoffending.
item.content:encoded:
One hundred inmates at Buimo Correctional Institution in Morobe graduated from a pre-release training program, equipping them with practical skills, knowledge and confidence for life after release.

The program of eight weeks is aimed to support inmates to improve their livelihood opportunities, and reduce the risk of reoffending.

Delivered by the Papua New Guinea Correctional Service with local partner Necktop Training Centre, and supported by the Australian Government through the Australia- Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Partnership, the program covered financial literacy, spiritual development, practical life skills and vocational training.

Participants also gained hands-on skills in areas such as coconut oil processing, helping prepare them for income-generating opportunities following release.

Australian High Commission Minister-Counsellor, Elizabeth Le Bas, said, “Australia is proud to support Papua New Guinea-led efforts to strengthen rehabilitation through its long-standing partnership with the Papua New Guinea Correctional Services.”

“If people leave custody without the skills or support to rebuild their lives, the challenges that brought them there often remain.

“But when people leave better prepared for what comes next, everyone benefits. Families are stronger and communities are safer,” she said.

For graduate Sharon Kamu, the training marked the beginning of a new chapter. Released on the same day she completed the program; she said the training helped rebuild her confidence and equipped her with practical skills to manage her finances and prepare for the future.

“The training resurrected my dreams and reminded me there is always a second chance,” Ms Kamu said.

Buimo Correctional Institution Commander, Michael Wundia, congratulated the 100 graduates and acknowledged Australia’s support for the program.

He commended the training for giving participants practical skills to support themselves, their families and communities after release. “Use these skills well, be good citizens and make the most of this opportunity when you return to your communities,” Mr Wundia said.

The Australia PNG Law and Justice Partnership is a PNG law and justice sector-led initiative, with programs prioritised through the National Coordinating Mechanism and delivered in partnership with sector agencies.

item.title: OFC Pro League set for Season 2 as all eight clubs approved for 2027 licensing

This milestone provides a strong base for the continued growth of the OFC Pro League, with all eight clubs demonstrating that they can meet the minimum requirements
item.content:encoded:
The OFC Pro League is getting set for a second season, with all eight clubs from the inaugural 2026 competition receiving approval for their 2027 Club Licence applications from the OFC Executive Committee which met in Fiji this month.

This milestone provides a strong base for the continued growth of the OFC Pro League, with all eight clubs demonstrating that they can meet the minimum requirements outlined in the OFC Professional League Club Licensing Regulations.

Club licensing is a critical part of the OFC Pro League framework, ensuring participating clubs continue to develop the structures, governance and standards required to compete at the professional level.

Following approval of their applications, the eight clubs will now progress through to the next stage of the process to confirm their participation, with additional requirements to be fulfilled before the process is completed ahead of the 2027 season.

For Papua New Guinea, PNG Hekari FC will once again participate in the second season of the OFC Pro League set to kick off next February.

Head of OFC Pro League, Stuart Larman, said the approval of all eight applications demonstrated the commitment of the clubs to building a stronger professional football environment across Oceania.

“Reaching Season 2 is an important moment for the OFC Pro League and for the continued development of professional football in the region,” Larman said.

“Having all eight clubs approved at this stage reflects the commitment they have made to meeting the standards required to operate at this level.

“This is about more than simply preparing for another season – it is about building strong, sustainable independent clubs that can contribute to the future of football across Oceania.

“We now look forward to working closely with the clubs as they complete the remaining participation requirements and prepare for what promises to be another exciting chapter for the league.”

The second season will build on the foundations established during the competition’s inaugural campaign, the title claimed by Auckland FC, providing a platform for clubs and players to compete at the highest level of club football in the Oceania region, meeting the vision of the OFC Exco.

Details of Season 2 dates, host countries, and venues will be released shortly.

item.title: New ventilators to support patients during air evacuations
item.description: Patients who become critically ill during medical evacuations will have access to advanced breathing support through four new ventilators provided to Manolos Aviation. The hospital-grade equipment will be used for patients who are unconscious or unable to breathe adequately on their own. Manolos Aviation managing director Captain Jurgen Ruh says the ventilators will strengthen the company’s abilit
item.content:encoded:
Patients who become critically ill during medical evacuations will have access to advanced breathing support through four new ventilators provided to Manolos Aviation.

The hospital-grade equipment will be used for patients who are unconscious or unable to breathe adequately on their own. Manolos Aviation managing director Captain Jurgen Ruh says the ventilators will strengthen the company’s ability to care for patients during flights.

“Being able to ventilate a patient gives us a much better option when treating someone who is critically ill during an aeromedical evacuation,” Ruh said.

Manolos Aviation has provided medical evacuation services for 16 years. Ruh said the ventilators may only be needed four or five times a year, but they are important to have available when a critically ill patient requires breathing support.

The four ventilators are valued at about K50,000 each and were provided by the Australian Government. Australian Consul General Brenton Kanowski. said the equipment would strengthen the capacity of medical teams to provide respiratory support during critical care and medical evacuations.

Medical staff have also received training in the use of the equipment from Australian Defence Force personnel and Australian nurse volunteer Sister Laura, who works at Angau Hospital. The ventilators will also complement Manolos Aviation’s developing clinic at the old airstrip in Lae and its helicopter aeromedical operations.

The Australian Government says the support is aimed at strengthening emergency and critical-care capacity in Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Celebration mode gains momentum for DWU’s 30th Anniversary
item.description: The Divine Word University has begun public awareness activities in the lead up to its 30th Anniversary, Festival of Legacy and Vision, with vibrant motorcades held in Rabaul, Port Moresby and Madang, bringing together staff, students, alumni, cultural groups and supporters in colourful displays of pride, unity and community spirit. The motorcade is served under the theme, “Celebrating 30 years of
item.content:encoded:
The Divine Word University has begun public awareness activities in the lead up to its 30th Anniversary, Festival of Legacy and Vision, with vibrant motorcades held in Rabaul, Port Moresby and Madang, bringing together staff, students, alumni, cultural groups and supporters in colourful displays of pride, unity and community spirit.

The motorcade is served under the theme, “Celebrating 30 years of Excellence, Service and Transformation to raise awareness of the university’s upcoming anniversary.

The Rabaul campus began its celebrations on August 3 with a motorcade through the Tokua and Vunapope areas. On August 4, students from the Kabaleo Teachers’ College showcased their creativity through songs and artwork, whilst students from St. Mary’s School of Nursing paraded and demonstrated the various areas of nursing service as part of the celebrations.

The Port Moresby campus, however; commenced its anniversary activities last weekend with a successful motorcade through the nation’s capital, drawing participation from staff, students, alumni and supporters. The event provided an opportunity to celebrate the University’s achievement over the past three decades, whilst also strengthening connections with the wider community and inviting the public to participate in the upcoming anniversary celebrations.

As part of the awareness campaign, information was also shared about key events for the Festival of Legacy and Vision, including the Foundation Day Exhibition, Entertainment Program, and Corporate Dinner.

In Madang, the University’s founding campus continued the momentum on Monday, 16th August, with a vibrant motorcade that travelled through key locations of town. The motorcade featured vehicles adorned with DWU 30th Anniversary, banners and flags, whilst students proudly carried anniversary flags and cultural groups showcased traditional performances.

Accompanied by music and public announcements, the procession highlighted DWU’s contribution to nation-building and community development through education over the past three decades.

Students also proudly participated in attire representing their various fields of study and future professions, showcasing the University’s diverse academic discipline and the roles its graduates continue to play in PNG’s workforce.

The enthusiastic response from residents and business houses along the route of the motorcade reflected the strong relationship between the University and the people of Madang.

Meanwhile, University President, Professor Fr. Philip Gibbs said the anniversary celebrations provide an opportunity to reflect on the University’s journey and its contribution to producing graduates who continue to serve communities throughout Papua New Guinea and beyond.

“For 30 years, DWU has remained committed to providing quality education, grounded in competency, integrity, and service. This anniversary is a celebration not only for the institution but of the thousands of graduates, staff, benefactors and communities who have contributed to our growth and success,” he said.

The celebrations will culminate in the Festival of Legacy and Vision at the DWU Madang campus from August 20- 22nd.

The three- day festival will feature academic and faculty exhibitions, cultural performances, alumni activities, scholarship showcases, tree planting initiatives, entertainment, and a gala dinner, bringing together alumni, students, staff, partners and supporters from across the country and abroad.

At the Port Moresby campus, celebrations will continue with a Foundation Day Exhibition and Entertainment Program, at the Taurama Aquatic Centre on Friday, 21 August, followed by a Corporate Dinner at the Dynasty Restaurant, Vision City Mall on Saturday, 22 August. The Corporate Dinner will provide opportunity for alumni, corporate partners, friends and supporters to come together in recognition of the University’s achievements and contributions to national development.

The Wewak campus, with teacher and nursing training, is preparing for 3 days of celebrations from September 14- 16, to coincide with the nation’s 51st independence anniversary.

As DWU marks its 30th anniversary, the institution also reaffirms its commitment to excellence in higher education, research, leadership development and community engagement, whilst continuing to transform lives and contribute meaningfully to the future of Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Oro rugby league gets boost
item.description: The Oro Rugby Football League Association (ORFLA) has received a K60,000 financial boost from its Patron and Member for Ijivitari, David Arore, as part of his K100,000 commitment towards supporting the continued development of grassroots rugby league in Oro Province. The cheque was presented to A16 Trading, the association’s official club uniform supplier, during a presentation witnessed by ORFLA
item.content:encoded:
The Oro Rugby Football League Association (ORFLA) has received a K60,000 financial boost from its Patron and Member for Ijivitari, David Arore, as part of his K100,000 commitment towards supporting the continued development of grassroots rugby league in Oro Province.

The cheque was presented to A16 Trading, the association’s official club uniform supplier, during a presentation witnessed by ORFLA President Stephen Kila Pat, PNGRFL Southern Confederate Officer Karo Kauna Jnr and Referees Director George Kadui.

Mr. Arore said the funding was part of his commitment to strengthening rugby league and creating better opportunities for young players across Oro Province.

“My commitment is to support the growth of rugby league in Oro.

This K60,000 is the first part of the K100,000 commitment, and I want to see our clubs properly equipped and our young players given the opportunity to develop,” Mr Arore said.

ORFLA President Stephen Kila Pat thanked the Patron and Ijivitari MP for honouring his commitment and directly supporting the association.

“We sincerely thank our Patron for backing his words with financial support.

“This assistance will go a long way in equipping our clubs and strengthening rugby league at the grassroots level,” Mr Kila Pat said.

Kila Pat also acknowledged Oro Governor, Gary Juffa for providing vital logistical support during the recently concluded coaching and referees’ clinics.

ORFLA is working towards affiliating three additional leagues by 2027, as it continues to strengthen the sport across the province and lay the foundation for a potential future franchise opportunity in the Digicel ExxonMobil Cup.

The association is also expected to make further announcements in the coming days following consultations with the PNGRFL executive team.

The K60,000 contribution marks the first instalment of Mr. Arore’s K100,000 commitment and is expected to assist clubs with uniforms and other requirements as the association continues developing rugby league at the grassroots level.

item.title: Police work to keep public and visitors safe at Hagen Show
item.description: For thousands of people who came to enjoy the 66th Mt Hagen Culture and Agriculture Show from the 14th-16th August 2026, the focus was on colourful costumes, traditional dances, music and meeting people from different parts of Papua New Guinea and overseas. But behind the celebrations, police officers were also working throughout the show to make sure people could enjoy the event safely.
item.content:encoded:
For thousands of people who came to enjoy the 66th Mt Hagen Culture and Agriculture Show from the 14th-16th August 2026, the focus was on colourful costumes, traditional dances, music and meeting people from different parts of Papua New Guinea and overseas.

But behind the celebrations, police officers were also working throughout the show to make sure people could enjoy the event safely.

Police were visible around Queen’s Park and other parts of Mt Hagen City, helping manage crowds, monitor movement and respond to incidents.

For many families, the presence of police provided a sense of security as they moved around the busy showground.

The three-day event attracted large crowds, including international visitors, cultural groups and people from across the Highlands region.

But the job for police did not end when the cultural performances finished.

Police were also needed to manage the movement of people leaving the show and to respond to law-and-order problems in the city.

The importance of that role became clear after some clashes were reported in parts of Mt Hagen city following the first and last days of the Show.

Police moved in and brought the situation under control.

For police officers on duty, the operation was not just about making arrests.

It was also about being present, talking to people, helping where needed and making sure families, visitors and cultural performers could return home safely.

"The Hagen Show is one of the biggest cultural events in the Highlands and attracts visitors from around the country and overseas. That makes security an important part of protecting not only the people attending the event, but also Mt Hagen's reputation as a destination for visitors," said Western Highlands Provincial Police Commander Chief Superintendent John Sagom who was in charge of the security element of the Show.

The Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary (RPNGC)h has previously highlighted community policing, public awareness and foot patrols as important parts of maintaining law and order in Mt Hagen City.

For the people attending the 66th Hagen Show, the police presence may have been something they barely noticed.

Hagen Show Chairman Pym Mamindi gave credit to the men and women in blue for providing security in and around the showground and also the city from the start of the show till the end and also extends his committee's gratitude locals boys who also provide security inside the singsing arena and local security firms as well.

" Our sincere thank you to the police and army who provided security that made it possible for the Show to end on a very high note. Also credit to those local security firms and local boys who also gave their best on making Show goers and especially tourists safe during the three days of Hagen Show," Mamindi says.

But for the officers working behind the scenes, keeping the crowds safe was part of making the celebration possible.

As the music, dancing and celebrations brought people together, police remained on the ground-watching, responding and helping thousands of people enjoy the Hagen Show safely.

item.title: New chapter for PNG’s standalone Medical University begins as Interim Council members sworn-in
item.description: Papua New Guinea has taken a significant step towards establishing its first standalone medical university in 50 years, following the swearing-in of the inaugural interim council of the Papua New Guinea University of Medicine and Health Sciences. NCD Senior Magistrate Billy Kidu officially administered the oath of office to the council, which will be responsible for establishing the university’s g
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea has taken a significant step towards establishing its first standalone medical university in 50 years, following the swearing-in of the inaugural interim council of the Papua New Guinea University of Medicine and Health Sciences.

NCD Senior Magistrate Billy Kidu officially administered the oath of office to the council, which will be responsible for establishing the university’s governance framework and overseeing the appointment of senior leadership, including the university president.

Former Finance Secretary Dr Ken Ngangan has been appointed interim council chairman, alongside members Ray Paul, Professor Ian Findlay, Health Secretary Pascoe Kase, and DHERST Secretary Leoni Baki.

The university is being established through the separation of the School of Medicine and Health Sciences from the University of Papua New Guinea.

Higher Education Minister Kinoka Feo said the new council carries a significant responsibility to deliver an institution that meets national expectations.

“The university must set high standards in medical education, clinical training, research and innovation.” he said.

Feo confirmed that the National Government has committed K2 billion for infrastructure development, with the first K50 million already released.

“Two major tenders are expected before the end of the year.” he added.

He further emphasised that infrastructure alone will not establish a world-class university.

“We must invest in academic staff, researchers and students.” he said.

He urged the council to develop an institution capable of serving the country for the next 50 to 100 years and producing graduates with internationally recognised qualifications.

UPNG Council Chairman Sir Robert Igara said the separation process must be managed with respect while maintaining a strong institutional partnership between UPNG and PNGUMHS.

“The transition is about the country and its people, not individuals holding positions.”he said.

Sir Robert proposed the development of a formal Memorandum of Agreement to ensure a long-term strategic partnership between the two institutions.

He also encouraged the new council that the two institutions must work together to build a strong foundation for the new university.

Meanwhile, Executive Dean of the School of Medicine and Health Sciences, Professor Nakapi Tefuarani, said the establishment of the new university presents a valuable opportunity to strengthen medical education, training, and healthcare delivery in Papua New Guinea.

He said: “This is an important opportunity to strengthen medical education, training and healthcare in our country.”

Interim council chairman Dr Ken Ngangan assured the government that the council is committed to fulfilling its mandate.

“We will work together to deliver on our responsibilities.” Dr Ngangan said.

The council will now focus on establishing the university’s governance structures, leadership systems, academic frameworks, and infrastructure to support the development of future generations of health professionals.

It is anticipated that the university will start enrolling first intakes in 2027.
